label: Hypnotized by her own partner / husband — 19 Nov 2026 follow-up
group_title: Female character hypnotized by her own partner or husband
description: Worldwide follow-up pass (19 Nov 2026 PT) for screen, short-form and AI-attributed works in which an adult female character is hypnotized by her own husband, boyfriend, fiancé, lover or ex (not a stranger, hired therapist, neighbor, or occult possessor). Possession, figurative 'hypnotized by his personality', drug/chip control without explicit hypnosis, and minors are excluded. New titles are added as standalone records under existing categories only (wife, partner-control, wife-hypnotized, and other existing keys when they fit). Family outcomes come from the cited plot sources; 'unknown' / 'not stated' where the sources are silent. TikTok and Instagram were searched via public web results only.

records.title: Cheers — "Veggie-Boyd"
records.meta: US television sitcom episode · NBC, 22 Nov 1990 · English · Cheers season 9, episode 10 · dir. James Burrows · written by Dan Staley and Rob Long
records.character: Dr. Lilith Sternin-Crane (Bebe Neuwirth), psychiatrist, wife of Dr. Frasier Crane
records.mechanism: Literal hypnosis: Frasier had previously hypnotized Lilith as a prank and planted trigger words that still work in the episode
records.summary: In this NBC Cheers episode, psychiatrist Frasier Crane hypnotizes bartender Woody Boyd so Woody will like a health drink he is advertising. When Lilith mocks the use of hypnosis, Frasier reveals that he recently hypnotized his wife as a party prank. Spoken cues still put her into brief, comic trances on screen (she removes her shoes at 'brie cheese,' begins to unbutton her blouse at 'tambourine,' and sings 'Tomorrow' at 'tractor'). The couple are already married and already have a son; the cited sources do not mention a pregnancy in this episode.
records.already_married_note: Yes — Lilith and Frasier married in 1988 (established in Cheers, 'Our Hourly Bread') and are still married in this 22 Nov 1990 episode; they later divorce in 1993
records.pregnancy_note: No pregnancy for Lilith is mentioned in the cited episode sources. Their son Frederick was already born in 1989, in the earlier episode 'The Stork Brings a Crane'.
records.kids_note: Wikipedia lists only one child for Lilith: Frederick Crane, her son with Frasier. No children from before that marriage are mentioned.
records.kids_together_note: Yes — they have a son, Frederick, born 1989, the year before this episode. After they later divorce, Lilith continues to raise him in Boston and they remain his parents.
records.fit_note: Adult married woman hypnotized by her own husband; the on-screen trance cues in this episode are a comic prank he had already planted.
records.evidence: Wikipedia season-9 episode listing (title, air date, writers, director) + Forever Dreaming episode transcript (Frasier says he hypnotized Lilith; the trigger words are spoken and she responds) + TV Tropes recap and IMDb character quotes confirming the same cues.
records.provenance: Partner-hypnosis follow-up pass, 19 Nov 2026 PT (adult women only; existing Cheers series card about Carla's pregnancies is a different storyline and is not overwritten)
